title: Large-vocabulary forensic pathological analyses via prototypical cross-modal contrastive learning
study_context: SongCi: forensic vision-language model pretrained on multicenter postmortem WSI, gross descriptions and diagnostic outcomes.
population_or_data: SongCi: forensic vision-language model pretrained on multicenter postmortem WSI, gross descriptions and diagnostic outcomes.
task: SongCi: forensic vision-language model pretrained on multicenter postmortem WSI, gross descriptions and diagnostic outcomes.
method: Prototypical and cross-modal contrastive representation learning; forensic validation and reported clinical-pathology transfer benchmarks.
main_findings: SongCi learned representations from postmortem WSI and text; the main article also reports transfer evaluation on three clinical WSI datasets and five patch datasets, beyond forensic tasks.
limitations: Selected-page review, not full-paper audit. PDF pages 1, 10, 17 and extracted text visually checked on 2026-10-07.

Clinical transfer benchmarks concern tumor/clinical pathology, not heart-transplant biopsy rejection. Main-text report only: Supplementary Tables 9-10, overlap controls, tuning details and quantitative transfer results were not audited. Does not show benefit over current UNI v2 or justify training on held-out SMC patients.
does_not_establish: Clinical transfer benchmarks concern tumor/clinical pathology, not heart-transplant biopsy rejection. Main-text report only: Supplementary Tables 9-10, overlap controls, tuning details and quantitative transfer results were not audited. Does not show benefit over current UNI v2 or justify training on held-out SMC patients.
relevance_to_project: A more direct precedent that autopsy-derived representations can be evaluated on clinical pathology tasks, motivating a controlled source-to-target comparison.
